label: Superheroes
rubric: Powers & abilities · Cultural icon status · Story impact · Fan popularity
note: Spans American comics, manga and anime, and screen originals rather than any one publisher, so ratings weigh a hero's standing in the culture at large rather than their rank within their own line.

entries.name: Superman
entries.rationale: The one every other cape is measured against — the character who invented the whole idea.

entries.name: Batman
entries.rationale: No powers, no limits: the detective whose preparation and will make him the equal of gods.

entries.name: Spider-Man
entries.rationale: The most recognizable hero on earth, beloved for carrying great power alongside ordinary problems.

entries.name: Goku
entries.rationale: The Saiyan who taught global pop culture what a power-up is, and never stopped raising the ceiling.

entries.name: Wonder Woman
entries.rationale: The Amazon warrior who has stood as comics' defining heroine for over eighty years.

entries.name: Iron Man
entries.rationale: The genius-billionaire in the armour who launched the modern superhero movie era single-handed.

entries.name: Naruto Uzumaki
entries.rationale: The outcast who talked his way to the top — the underdog arc that defined a whole generation of manga.

entries.name: Captain America
entries.rationale: A living symbol of conviction, defined less by the shield than by refusing to put it down.

entries.name: Monkey D. Luffy
entries.rationale: A rubber-limbed pirate captain fronting the best-selling comic series in history, by a wide margin.

entries.name: Wolverine
entries.rationale: The clawed antihero whose brutal edge made him an instant fan favourite across five decades.

entries.name: Hulk
entries.rationale: Raw destructive force wrapped around a tragedy — strength as a curse rather than a gift.

entries.name: Thor
entries.rationale: The God of Thunder, folding Norse myth into some of the genre's largest-scale action.

entries.name: The Flash
entries.rationale: The Scarlet Speedster, whose runs rewrote continuity itself more than once.

entries.name: Saitama
entries.rationale: A hero so strong the joke is his boredom — the sharpest satire the genre has produced.

entries.name: Black Panther
entries.rationale: King of Wakanda, whose cultural significance reached far beyond the comic-book page.

entries.name: Deadpool
entries.rationale: The fourth-wall-breaking Merc with a Mouth who turned irreverence into a box-office phenomenon.

entries.name: Sailor Moon
entries.rationale: Built the magical-girl team template that a thousand series have run on ever since.

entries.name: Green Lantern
entries.rationale: A ring powered by willpower alone, limited only by what its bearer can imagine.

entries.name: Doctor Strange
entries.rationale: The Sorcerer Supreme, guarding reality from threats the strongest fists cannot touch.

entries.name: All Might
entries.rationale: The Symbol of Peace — a deliberate love letter to American superheroes, drawn better than most.

entries.name: Aquaman
entries.rationale: King of Atlantis, rehabilitated from long-running punchline into a genuine heavyweight.

entries.name: Astro Boy
entries.rationale: Tezuka's atomic-powered boy robot: the foundation stone the entire manga industry was built on.

entries.name: Edward Elric
entries.rationale: Equivalent exchange, an automail arm, and the most tightly plotted hero's journey in manga.

entries.name: Storm
entries.rationale: A weather-commanding X-Man, worshipped as a goddess and among the most powerful mutants drawn.

entries.name: Ichigo Kurosaki
entries.rationale: A substitute Soul Reaper with an oversized blade and a decade of genre-defining fights.

entries.name: Daredevil
entries.rationale: The blind Man Without Fear, patrolling Hell's Kitchen on heightened senses and sheer stubbornness.

entries.name: Supergirl
entries.rationale: The last daughter of Krypton, carrying the same power with none of the settled certainty.

entries.name: Miles Morales
entries.rationale: A widely celebrated Spider-Man who expanded who gets to wear the mask, then earned the spotlight.

entries.name: Izuku Midoriya
entries.rationale: Born powerless in a world of powers, and the better hero for having had to earn it.

entries.name: Nightwing
entries.rationale: The sidekick who grew up and out, becoming the most beloved leader in the DC universe.

entries.name: Raven
entries.rationale: A half-demon empath holding her own bloodline at bay — the dark heart of the Teen Titans.

entries.name: Captain Marvel
entries.rationale: One of the most powerful heroes in the cosmos, able to stand toe-to-toe with world-enders.

entries.name: Tanjiro Kamado
entries.rationale: Relentless kindness with a blade, fronting one of the biggest box-office phenomena in anime history.

entries.name: Invincible
entries.rationale: A teenage hero whose story turned the superhero coming-of-age tale genuinely brutal.

entries.name: Shazam
entries.rationale: A boy who says one word and becomes a god — and once outsold Superman on the newsstand.

entries.name: Spawn
entries.rationale: A murdered soldier back from hell — the flagship of the independent comics boom.

entries.name: Hellboy
entries.rationale: A demon raised to fight for the good guys, filing his horns down out of pure spite.

entries.name: Green Arrow
entries.rationale: A billionaire archer with a social conscience and a quiver of increasingly improbable trick arrows.

entries.name: Mob
entries.rationale: An overwhelmingly powerful esper who would genuinely rather just get better at talking to people.

entries.name: Mr. Incredible
entries.rationale: Superheroics as a midlife crisis — the film that got the genre right before the genre did.

entries.name: Martian Manhunter
entries.rationale: The last Martian: telepath, shapeshifter, and the quiet emotional core of the Justice League.

entries.name: Vash the Stampede
entries.rationale: The sixty-billion-double-dollar man who refuses to kill, and pays for that choice constantly.

entries.name: Gon Freecss
entries.rationale: A cheerful boy hunting his father through the most rigorously designed power system in manga.

entries.name: The Rocketeer
entries.rationale: A stunt pilot, a stolen jetpack, and the most gorgeous art deco in comics.

entries.name: Judge Dredd
entries.rationale: Judge, jury and executioner — a satire so deadpan that plenty of readers still miss the joke.

entries.name: Static
entries.rationale: Milestone's electromagnetic teenager, and the most enduring hero to come out of that line.

entries.name: Yusuke Urameshi
entries.rationale: A delinquent who died saving a child and got the job of Spirit Detective as thanks.

entries.name: Zatanna
entries.rationale: A stage magician whose backwards-spoken spells are entirely real, and rarely under control.

entries.name: Blue Beetle
entries.rationale: An alien scarab bonded to an ordinary teenager who mostly just wants it to stop talking.

entries.name: Ben 10
entries.rationale: A kid with a watch that turns him into ten different aliens — a whole generation's first hero.
